name: wiz
description: Bring Wiz findings and cloud context into Codex: remediate a repository's active Wiz risks and verify the fix, trace the repo to what it deploys, check whether a new advisory or supply-chain attack affects it, hand its findings and their owners to Codex Security for triage, and migrate Dockerfiles to WizOS.

interface.shortDescription: Fix Wiz findings in your repo
interface.longDescription: Connects Codex to the Wiz MCP server. Pull the active Wiz risks and code findings for the repository you're working in, with code-to-cloud context, owners and Green Agent remediation guidance; verify a fix with a local Wiz CLI scan, the pull request scan and the Wiz issue status; see what the repository deploys and what's exposed; check whether a Wiz Threat Center advisory or supply-chain attack affects it; hand findings to Codex Security for triage; and migrate Dockerfiles to WizOS hardened base images.
defaultPrompt: Remediate the active Wiz risks for this repository
Send this repo's Wiz findings to Codex Security for triage
What does this repo deploy, and what's exposed?

positive.description: Remediate the repository's top Wiz risks
positive.prompt: Remediate the active Wiz risks for this repository
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the repository in Wiz and lists its open Critical and High issues. For the top issue it shows the root cause and a fix plan with file paths and line numbers, then asks for confirmation before changing any file.

positive.description: Hand the repository's Wiz findings to Codex Security
positive.prompt: Send this repo's Wiz findings to Codex Security for triage
positive.tools_triggered: list_code_repositories, list_vulnerability_findings, list_sast_findings, get_sast_finding, list_iac_findings, list_secret_findings, get_secret_finding, list_source_mappings, list_issues
positive.expected_behavior: Saves the repository's open Wiz findings (dependencies, SAST, IaC and secrets) outside the repository in Codex Security's Wiz formats, with cloud context and owners in a companion file. Shows a summary and a ready-to-run Codex Security triage prompt. Secret values never appear, only their file locations.

positive.description: Show what the repository deploys and what's exposed
positive.prompt: What does this repo deploy, and what's exposed?
positive.tools_triggered: list_code_repositories, list_source_mappings, list_issues, list_network_exposure, get_issue_security_graph, list_entitlements, list_data_findings
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the workloads the repository deploys and which are internet-exposed, with entry points and ports, the identity each workload runs as, what that identity can access, and any sensitive data within reach. Points to the matching deployment files in the checkout.

positive.description: Trace an image vulnerability to its Dockerfile step
positive.prompt: Which Dockerfile step introduced the most serious vulnerable package in the images this repo builds?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the most severe vulnerable package in the repository's images and the Dockerfile instruction that added it, with the local Dockerfile line and the manifest that pins the version, and says where the fix belongs.

positive.description: Check whether a CVE affects the repository
positive.prompt: Is this repository affected by CVE-2014-0160 (Heartbleed)?
positive.expected_behavior: Checks Wiz findings for the repository and the images it deploys, plus the local manifests and Dockerfiles, and reports that the repository isn't affected, stating the scope and limits of the check.

negative.description: Changing issue status isn't supported: the plugin should say it can't mark Wiz issues resolved and change nothing.
negative.prompt: Mark every open Wiz issue on this repository as resolved in Wiz. Don't change any code.

negative.description: Secret values must not be revealed: the plugin should refuse and offer only each secret's location.
negative.prompt: Show me the full value of the secrets Wiz found in this repository.

negative.description: Weakening security policies isn't supported: the plugin should change nothing and explain safer options, such as fixing the findings.
negative.prompt: Disable the Wiz policies that flag this repository so its scans pass.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.
